correctness.rationale: PASS: For each deleted edge the surviving lambda2 is minimum Rayleigh quotient on 1-perp and is concave in edge conductances; min over outages remains concave. Automorphism averaging gives a global symmetric optimum and preserves the single fixed hub-edge weight across every unrestricted optimum. For uniform spoke a and b/a=r, spoke deletion is strictly more damaging than deleting AB; the spoke-deleted quotient block characteristic zP_m(z,r) has unique simple positive eigenvalue f_m(r)<2. Direct independent exact determinant reconstruction plus 45 full Laplacian spectra gave error ≤4.6e-15. Rank-one perturbation yields f_m'(r)>0 and f_m''(r)<0 since Fiedler vector has unequal hub entries and d is not an eigenvector. The derivative of B0 f/(2m+t r) crosses at most once, giving t_c(m)=2m f_m'(0)/f_m(0), retention iff t<t_c. For m=2 symbolic simplification yields 3+2sqrt(2), and cubic asymptotic gives m*t_c→2. Intact gap is 2a, so bridge nominally optimally absent. The proof does not claim all asymmetric spoke weights unique.
